messages:
Lina (product): quick sync — customer A just asked for a private deploy guarantee: rolling upgrades with preserved customer egress IPs and optional customer-managed NAT. they want a clear SLA and a migration path from our current bundle to a slim agent. TL;DR: how do we prioritize and what are the non-negotiables?
Matt (eng): agree this is common ask. big constraints: KV cache invalidation during rolling upgrade, and model-serving pods need graceful drain. we have two technical paths: operator-shim (controller handles in-cluster upgrade choreography) or sidecar-based rolling replace. operator gives us more control for canary -> full rollout.
Sarah (netops): preserving egress IP is the kicker. many customers will not accept SNAT changes. we should support both: 1) customer-controlled NAT (preferred), 2) static egress via our relay (fallthrough). also need clear notes on BGP vs static routes for peering.
Jill (devops): from packaging POV: we can offer three installer presets: full (includes relay+metrics), slim (agent minimal, expects customer NAT), and airgap (tarball + offline deps). slim reduces surface area but requires documented hooks for egress pinning + post-install IP validation.
Lina (product): sounds like we can frame launch criteria: - rolling upgrade without >1min p99 spike - egress IP preserved for pinned tenants - installer preset "slim" supported and validated by field test on 2 customers - documented rollback steps + canary checklist
Matt (eng): can we validate with a small spike test: create test harness that simulates 100 tenants with pinned egress and run canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%? also need an operator health-check endpoint: `/health/upgrade-ready` that returns graceful drain status.
Sarah (netops): For documentation, include a short runbook for customer NAT: BGP example + iptables fallback. sample for BGP advertise: `neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65000` and sample validation command `curl -sS https://ifconfig.me` (note privacy).
Jill (devops): packaging note: slim mode flags proposal:```yaml
installer_mode: slim
preserve_egress: true
relay_enabled: false
```. also add a `--force-ip-check` post-install step.
Lina (product): prioritization ask: do we slot this in Q2 core infra (high) or Q3 field polish? i'd argue high — drives a lot of enterprise commitments. need rough estimate to include in roadmap.
Matt (eng): rough effort: operator + canary infra ~4 eng-sprints (2 engs), packaging + installer presets ~1 sprint (1 eng), netops docs + tests ~0.5 sprint. total ~5.5 sprint-equivalents.
Sarah (netops): plus field validation with customer A and customer C — plan 2 validation windows (one for BGP, one for NAT). expect 1 week per window.
Lina (product): action items: @Matt -> PRD stub with canary test plan by Tue. @Jill -> slim installer flags + validation script by Fri. @Sarah -> draft egress runbook and BGP examples by Thu. @ops-bot -> create a tracking ticket in #shiproom with these owners. If anyone disagrees, speak now.
Matt (eng): acknowledged, starting PRD stub.
Jill (devops): will prototype `--force-ip-check` tomorrow.
Sarah (netops): adding BGP + iptables snippets to draft.
ops-bot: created ticket RDW-5243: "private-deploy: rolling-upgrade + egress-preservation" assigned to Lina, Matt, Jill, Sarah. :white_check_mark:
Lina (product): thanks all — i'll fold estimates into the roadmap doc and ping legal for SLA language. we should plan a 30-min walkthrough next Mon.
Matt (eng): +1 for walkthrough.
Jill (devops): added to calendar.
Sarah (netops): thanks — will pull sample configs from field.
Lina (product): end.
